key: He who has killed multitudes of men should weep for them with the bitterest grief; and the victor in battle has his place (rightly) according to those rites.
s: The chapter ends on the dead of war; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 31, reads the weeping as grief that thin virtue, unable to transform by the Tao, harmed the innocent, and the victor’s white mourning as fitting one who strikes only of necessity.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 31, zh.wikisource (a normalised text), revision 2019760 (2021)

evidence.words: 傷己德薄，不能以道化人，而害無辜之民 … 將軍居喪主禮之位，素服而哭之，明君子貴德而賤兵，不得以而誅不祥
evidence.gloss: He grieves that his own virtue is thin, that he could not transform people by the Tao and so harmed innocent people … the general takes the chief mourner’s place, wears plain white and weeps, making plain that the superior man honours virtue and holds arms cheap, and punishes the ill-omened only when he cannot avoid it.
